messages:
maria: FYI we saw a spike in CPU-fallbacks for a subset of requests hitting AMD nodes around 2:14am UTC. profile attached in thread.
jonathan: Which model + seq lengths? any pattern on batch sizes?
maria: Mostly gpt-medium-ish (7B family) with seq_len distribution that has a small tail > 2048. batch sizes were 1-4.
akshay: Can you paste the profiler snippet? curious if the runtime picked a different attention kernel.
maria: Sure — pasted below:
```
[PROF] model load: kernels found: 51
[PROF] runtime: requested kernel(attn_fwd, amdgpu, seq=4096) -> NOT_FOUND
[PROF] routing: fallback -> cpu_attn_ref
[METRIC] extra_latency = +48ms per token
```
sara: Hmm NOT_FOUND on attn_fwd for seq 4096. That suggests our kernel build table doesn't include large-seq kernels for that AMDKMD version. driver was rocm-5.5.2.
ryan: Did we recently change the kernel naming convention? autotuner could have skipped some binary combos.
akshay: I dug into the kernel catalog: we store entries keyed by (arch, driver_tag, opset, seq_bucket). The probe we do at model load queries the local kernel cache; if a bucket is missing we mark it as unavailable but we don't currently expose that to the router beyond a binary OK/missing flag.
maria: Right — the router uses simple compatibility ordering: prefer amdgpu kernels > cuda > cpu. It doesn't consider that only small-seq kernels exist. So for seq=4096 we incorrectly assumed amdgpu support and then runtime discovered NOT_FOUND during kernel selection and fell back mid-exec.
jonathan: That mid-exec discovery is bad — costly. Can we add a preflight probe for sequence-bucket coverage per device at model load, and make routing consult that map before routing requests?
akshay: Proposed quick mitigation: when model instance starts, run probe: for seq_bucket in [64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096] call kernel_lookup(arch, opset, seq_bucket). Cache result in node metadata and expose via /node-kernel-map.
sara: +1. Also add a tiebreaker: if target device has partial coverage and request.seq_len in an uncovered bucket, route to next best device (older GPU with kernel), not fallback to CPU.
ryan: We should be careful about throughput — routing around GPUs can increase network hop count. Maybe add a safety config: "prefer_local": true/false and a threshold for latency increase.
infra-bot: queued task #4521: rocm kernel probe endpoint + node metadata -> assigned to akshay. ETA 2d.
akshay: Implementation note: probe should be idempotent and light — only check kernel manifest hashes, not build binaries. Example probe call:
```
curl -s http://node:9000/internal/kernel-map?arch=amdgpu&opset=1.2
# returns: {"seq_buckets": [64,128,256,512,1024], "kernel_hash": "abc123"}
```
jonathan: For safety, add a graceful-degradation flag: if a request hits an uncovered bucket and there is no alternate GPU, allow CPU fallback but emit a high-severity log and a metric to trigger autoscale.
maria: Also update the autotuner: when generating kernel candidates, prioritize producing a minimal set covering high-percentile seq_buckets per customer traces. We waste build time on rare combos. Need histograms from Optimize.
sara: Another thing — KV cache path diverges for >2048 sequences, and we saw extra mem-copies during fallback. We should ensure caching layer marks small/large seq paths so router knows memory profile too.
akshay: I'll add node-kernel-map to the /nodes API and include seq_bucket coverage + estimated mem footprint per bucket. That should let the router do cost-aware routing.
ryan: After probe + router change, let's run a canary: route 5% traffic off the original devices and monitor token latency and error rates for 24h.
maria: Agreed. timeline: probe + metadata (48h), router consult (24h), canary (1 day), rollout. I'll create a PR for the probe spec.
jonathan: Thanks. Also add a perf-regression alert rule: sudden increase in "kernel_not_found" errors per node -> page infra if rate > 5/min.
maria: adding to runbook. :memo:
infra-bot: task #4521 updated: probe endpoint implemented PR created -> https://git.company/repo/pull/789
maria: Nice. Once PR merges we'll schedule canary. :eyes:
